# Day 40: Course-level check 1, facts and opinions

## Teacher page

### Before class
Read teacher-only key-d040.md. Prepare Source A and Source B as printed below. Keep them unseen until this sitting. Add the three component columns to day 39's record. Keep the map and leaflet legible in enlarged copies. Plan thirty minutes after class for thirty papers, then select one priority per child across both check days.

### The day
#### 3 min. Opening
Day 39's assessment is held for return on day 41. Name the map check without showing its answers. Explain that Source A is a made-up leaflet for imagined travelers. Its place statements concern real geography; its opinions belong to an invented writer. Source B was made separately. Explain pointing, drawing or dictated access; no child must disclose travel or family experiences.

#### 12 min. Read and sort
Children read Source A and answer [[C1-E40-1]] alone. Give a neutral read-aloud or tracking support without stressing opinion words. This checks written day 21's distinction, not knowledge of a new place from memory. Every needed sentence is supplied. Leave Source B visible.

#### 12 min. Map evidence
Children answer [[C1-E40-2]] alone. They may annotate the river line and boundary instead of writing a full sentence. Ask no follow-up that supplies the map relationship. Record help actually given. No whole-class answer sharing.

#### 8 min. Source judgment
Children answer [[C1-E40-3]] independently. A preference does not make neighboring location statements false. Keep this explanation for feedback after collection, rather than coaching during the assessment.

#### 5 min. Collect
Children inspect their source labels and return papers. After class use shown, shown with help, not yet seen per component. Access alone does not reduce evidence. Combine results with day 39 and unresolved day 38 needs. One priority per child enters day 41; many means more than a third. No public totals.

### Other rooms
No device, visitor or outside photograph is needed. No printer: prepare the same leaflet and outline by hand before class. Read words neutrally; a scribe records the child's evidence exactly.

### At home
**Swap.** No printer: copy the short sources and trace the map before starting. No class record: keep both check papers together.
**Skip.** Group collection and public sharing.
- **3 min. Assessment reading.** Explain that the leaflet writer is made up.
- **12 min. Sort.** Your child reads Source A and answers [[C1-E40-1]] alone.
- **12 min. Evidence.** Keep Source B visible for [[C1-E40-2]]. Give no hints.
- **8 min. Judgment.** Your child completes [[C1-E40-3]].
- **5 min. Keep.** Put the paper beside day 39 work. Read key-d040.md privately afterward. Choose one next step for day 41.

### Shorter or longer
Retain all three components; use remaining minutes for neutral rereading. Longer: children improve clarity within their existing answers before collection.

### Words and supports
Review checkable, opinion and evidence from written days 21 and 22. A liking is not a reason. Supply enlarged labels, neutral reading and directed dictation. Grammar, spelling and travel knowledge do not determine the evidence judgment.

### Tomorrow
Day 41 returns day 39 and day 40 work privately. Response groups address error L, printed means proved; error D, repeated claim instead of separate evidence; error C, preference treated as fact; or error K, one opinion cancels everything. Combine these with map needs for one assigned route.

### Credit
Ours. Original leaflet and cartography. Source rows C1-geo-country, C1-geo-alaska, C1-geo-rivers and C1-yukon support the geographic statements. No source wording or images are copied.

## Student page
### Side 1
<style>body.student {font-size:14pt;line-height:1.25} body.student p {margin:.3em 0} body.student h1 {font-size:18pt;margin:.3em 0}</style>
**I can judge facts and opinions using evidence.**

**Source A: Travel leaflet.**
Maker: classroom writer, 2026. Audience: imagined travelers.
This leaflet and its writer are made up.

1. The Yukon River crosses Alaska.
2. Alaska has a coastline.
3. The Yukon is the loveliest river.
4. Every visitor should choose Alaska.

**Source B: Northwestern North America.**
Maker: classroom mapmaker, 2026. Audience: students checking locations.
The mapmaker used geographic records, not the leaflet.
